Expensify does pretty horrible categorization. It does a really good job at determining amount, but approx 70% of the time manages to screw up the categorization unless it's really obvious.

TL;DR: Expensify's deceptive mechanical turk army may have resulted in me coming within seconds of losing $30k, giving away PII to low-paid contract workers not bound to confidentiality via SmartScan.
Some of the receipts had enough info to identify people - store card numbers, buyer phone number, etc. My wife occasionally does mturk and lots of the tasks were Expensify receipts.

Lots of companies like Expensify, Bills.com, ReceiptHog use MTurk to extract data from financial documents. Accuracy is not 100% guaranteed and categorization is often off since the person doesn't know your purchase history.
I used expensify and it took like 20 mins to process a few receipt images.. I ended up doing it myself anyway.

Expensify's CEO sent a letter to every single person Expensify had an email for, even ground floor employees who just use the software, prior to the 2020 election urging them to vote for Biden. I will never give this company a single cent after that stunt.
When my startup was acquired, we had to migrate from using Expensify to SAP Concur. Lord, how I miss Expensify. It was the epitome of intuitive.

Anything that can reduce SAP Concur adoption is a win in my book. Expensify is so much nicer to use if you're on the hook for tracking your own expenses. I love that they'll scan receipts and enter the data for you.

I singlehandedly forced the replacement of Expensify at my company after dodgy billing practices - they incrementally raised our bill over eight months with no notification, then wouldn't issue a credit when I complained.

Having to fill in many forms this morning, I was marveling at how unnecessarily painful data entry is with Expensify. Pressing Enter on an autocomplete sometimes saves the whole expense and exits, other times it works as expected - totally inconsistent.
